parsed.summary: The Lean theorem states quadratic reciprocity for distinct odd primes p and q: (p/q)·(q/p) = (-1)^(⌊p/2⌋·⌊q/2⌋). Here legendreSym q p is (p/q) and legendreSym p q is (q/p). For odd p, natural-number division gives ⌊p/2⌋ = (p-1)/2, so the exponent matches the paper. No material caveat; the only subtlety is that the exponent uses truncating ℕ division, which is exact here.

glossary.plain: legendreSym p a is the Legendre symbol (a/p) for a prime p and an integer a, taking values in ℤ.

lean_claims.plain: For primes p ≠ q with p ≠ 2 and q ≠ 2: (p/q)·(q/p) = (-1)^(⌊p/2⌋·⌊q/2⌋) in ℤ.

paper_claims.plain: For distinct odd primes p, q: (p/q)(q/p) = (-1)^(((p-1)/2)((q-1)/2)).

coverage.why: Odd primes give ⌊p/2⌋ = (p-1)/2 exactly. Multiplication is commutative, so the order of the two symbols does not matter.

lint_verdicts.why: p and q are odd, so ℕ floor division p/2 equals (p-1)/2 exactly; nothing is truncated away.
